summary: NOAA confirmed July 2026 as the hottest month on record, with Midwest crops facing daytime highs near 110F. Rabo Research's Stephen Nicholson pointed to elevated overnight lows, rather than daytime peaks, as the mechanism: a decades-long rise in night-time temperatures denies crops recovery time after heat and disrupted pollination for a large share of this year's corn crop. This is the attribution mechanism behind the tip-back and missing kernel rows the Crop Tour scouts recorded in Nebraska and Illinois this week.
